name: AshCoveredHome
source:
An old building on a road blanketed in stony powder 
 
 The old neighborhood has not held up well. Back when I was a kid the worst thing around here was the raccoons, now every house has been an abandoned piece of rubble for years. Everything has become grey with ash. What used to be my childhood bastion is practically a junkyard now. Mailboxes, bicycles, forsaken cars, everything is blanketed in the smoky dust from the bombs.

Everything has become grey with ash. What used to be my childhood bastion is practically a junkyard now. Mailboxes, bicycles, forsaken cars, everything is blanketed in the smoky dust from the bombs. 
 
 I want to see home, what was home, a final time. Deserters never last long, they always get executed or expire in the wastes. Perhaps I have about forgotten deserters who fall victim to themselves. I have known a few. That is going to be my exit. 
 
 Raising my sullen head, I see the remains of my old home. Now a mausoleum to memory. Turning the knob, I can hear the wooden stress and the rust from the bolt grate against the frame. An unpleasant stillness billows through the house. Past the photos of better times, though we did n't know it then, past the kitchen, that used to feed a family of seven but now is only a home to roaches, and past the bedrooms, where when the world was too much we could retire for at least a little while. 
 
 But the world has changed 
 
 I unshoulder my rifle. Sliding back the bolt I see my death. As I sit down in my father's chair, before I can orient my weapon into the position that can fulfill its purpose, I hear a song played by a violin. 
 
 I look up and see a man in uniform missing the upper portion of his head sitting in the chair opposite of me playing a violin with one string, playing an adagio of tragic malice. I remember him. He was a violent, angry man in life, until the end, now his stare is somber, reticent. 
 
 He plays for a few more bars, maintaining this painful visual connection with me, then he gently places the instrument to his side and slinks back in his chair to the position I had seen him in when his gun had fulfilled its purpose. With that he was no longer a man again, just a corpse. 
 
 I look at my rifle and see the remorselessness of its form and its function. I think of the man who once was and is no longer. I make my decision. I orient my rifle precisely where I want it to go 
 
 *Author's Note: This really is n't my best work I feel. I had an idea for the first half and then I hit a block. Still please feel free to comment on what you liked or disliked and as always tell me if you see any mistakes*
retelling:
Perspective: The Man in Uniform, the deceased former resident of the house, playing the violin.

In a world shattered by war and destruction, I found myself in a forgotten corner, a place once bustling with life and love. The air was thick with dust and the scent of decay, yet my hands were guided by an unseen force to play the music that echoed through this desolate landscape.

I was once part of this family of seven, living under one roof, creating a symphony of laughter and tears. Now, I stand here alone, headless but still able to feel the memories seeping from every cracked wall and splintered piece of furniture. The house is now a mausoleum to memory, but my music breathes life into these silent halls.

Today, a stranger entered this forgotten home, drawn by the melody that I create. He carried the weight of his past and the burden of his sins, etched upon his weary face. His eyes were hollow, reflecting the ashen world outside, but there was something in him that yearned for more - a spark that refused to be extinguished.

As he walked through the rooms filled with roaches and decay, my music swelled, filling the silence. I played for him the tales of love and loss, of joy and sorrow, of life and death. And as he reached the father's chair where his former self would have sat, he paused, looking around at the crumbling remnants of a happier past.

In that moment, I felt something shift within him. He had come here seeking an escape from the pain of living, carrying a rifle to end his suffering. But in the silence and the melody, in the echoes of laughter and tears, he found a reason to live. And so, he put down his weapon, choosing life over death, just as I had once chosen my music over despair.

I continued playing, knowing that even after I cease to exist, my music will continue to resonate through this desolate landscape, offering hope to those who seek it and reminding them of the beauty that can be found in even the most broken of places.
